lines.text: Hobb was sitting by my brother's bed, across the city. Through his thread, I could feel what he was feeling. Maric was going.
The draught has reached his heart. Lucan, there's nothing anyone could carry to him in time. Not from here.
I had come all this way to steal a cure. Pure hollow-born aether. The thing the Order farmed in the dark.
And then I understood, sitting on that cold floor. I didn't need to steal it. I was it.
A Tide won't heal him unless he's bonded. He has to accept you, Lucan. He's refused you twice.
Then I'll ask a third time. Loudly.
I closed my eyes and found them. Sixty-three threads, strung across the night city. A line of little cold lights, from the cathedral to my father's door.
Like a bucket line at a fire. I had seen one save a grain store, once.
I poured a Tide into the nearest thread. And I pushed.
Hobb told me later what it looked like from the street. A light leaping from corner to corner across Aldcrown. Every worker it touched lit up like a lamp, gasped, and passed it on.
Mags said it went through her like hot soup on a cold night. She dropped both buckets.
It came in through my father's window, into Hobb. Hobb didn't understand it. He did it anyway. He laid his big sooty hands on my brother's chest.
And from the bottom of a vault, a mile away, I said the only thing I had left to say.
Accept it, idiot.
Maric told me afterwards he heard it as clearly as if I'd been standing over his bed. He said it was the rudest thing anyone had ever said to him.
...Fine. Fine, little brother.
A new thread ran out of me. Cold, like all the others. But it crackled, like a fire just catching.
In my father's house, the white fire went out of my brother like a fever breaking. And the old fire came back. Red and gold. His own.
My father didn't say a word, Hobb said. He just put his hand on Hobb's shoulder, and left it there.
In the vault, I opened my eyes. My hands were white to the wrist, and turning blue. I couldn't feel them. Nell's hand had found mine in her sleep. It was the only warm thing I could feel.
And in the silence afterwards, through the floor, from somewhere far below us, I heard someone humming.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and four, coming soon.
